svg.title: Speed against v0.6.1, one row per timing program
svg.desc: Timing set 2026-10-20-against-v0.6.1: v0.6.1 against main at 876247f, the first v0.7 speed package. 133 timed cases in 23 of 24 timing programs, one row per program in name order: the range from the lowest to the highest v0.6.1 median time divided by the new one over the cases of the program, and their median, on a log scale centred at 1 over the widest A/A noise band of those cases. Cases are grouped by timing program; per-case results are in docs/speed-results/2026-10-20-against-v0.6.1. 103 cases are faster beyond their A/A band, 18 slower beyond it (SHA-256 alone at 0.28 and 0.39) and 12 inside it. 22 of 23 timed programs printed the same output digest in all three trees. speed_top1_many has only a manifest: its API does not exist in v0.6.1, so the example does not build there. speed_tree_gates prints DIFFERENT_OUTPUT because it counts the files of the tree it runs in, and the two trees differ. Machine: AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, 24 hardware threads, 94 GiB RAM, Linux 6.17; load average 2.7 at the start, 12.6 to 19.4 at the end, from other work on the machine; not pinned to cores. Ratios of different programs are not comparable with each other; the output digests, not the timings, are the claim.
svg.text: SPEED · v0.6.1 AGAINST main AT 876247f · SET 2026-10-20-against-v0.6.1
133 timed cases in 23 of 24 timing programs: v0.6.1 time divided by the new time
One row per timing program: the range of its cases from min to max, and their median · cases grouped by timing program; per-case results are in docs/speed-results
A, A2: two checkouts of v0.6.1 · B: main at 876247f, the first v0.7 speed package · medians of 9 to 27 runs per case
Machine: AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370, 24 hardware threads, 94 GiB RAM, Linux 6.17 · not pinned to cores
Load: load average 2.7 at the start, 12.6 to 19.4 at the end, from other work on the machine
same output digest in A, A2 and B: 22 of 23
range of its cases, min to max: red below 1, blue above 1
widest A/A band of its cases: the noise to read it against

g.text: not built in v0.6.1: no timing

svg.text: Note 1 · speed_top1_many has only a manifest: its API does not exist in v0.6.1, so the example does not build there.
Note 2 · speed_tree_gates prints DIFFERENT_OUTPUT because it counts the files of the tree it runs in, and the two trees differ.

The machine was loaded and the runs were not pinned to cores, so each grey band, the A/A ratios of two copies of v0.6.1, is the noise to read a span against: samples of that noise, not a confidence interval.

A case counts as faster or slower only beyond its own band. Ratios of different programs are not comparable with each other: each program times its own work. The output digests, not the timings, are the claim.
